newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Ex-senator wounded, two mayors killed in Colombia.
newsitem.headline: Ex-senator wounded, two mayors killed in Colombia.

text.p: Unidentified gunmen on Sunday shot and wounded a former senator and her husband, a Protestant pastor, before fleeing on a public bus in Bogota, police said.

Claudia Rodriguez, a former Christian Democrat legislator, and husband Cesar Castellanos each suffered three gunshot wounds when two men on a motorcycle sprayed their car with bullets in a northern suburb of the capital. Both were in a stable condition in a Bogota clinic, hospital authorities said in a brief statement.
After opening fire on the couple, the assassins abandoned the motorcycle and flagged down a passing bus, Bogota police chief Gen. Teodoro Campo said.
He said the motive for the attack was not clear but it could be linked to the theft of one of the couple's vehicles earlier in the week.

In two separate incidents elsewhere in Colombia, Climaco Navarro Palacio, mayor of the town of Guatica in central Risaralda province, was shot and killed by 10 suspected leftist guerrillas, radio reported.

Local police chief Col. Jairo Ramirez said the mayor had been watching a soccer match, part of a so-called "sport for peace" tournament, when the rebels dragged him off into a nearby coffee plantation and killed him.

In southwest Huila province, Jose Luis Pena, mayor of the town of Acevedo, was murdered by two unidentified assasins, according to the Radionet radio network. The killing appeared to have been sparked by a personal dispute with other members of the town council, Radionet reported.
